solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Player doing a stretch by the book

parts.note: a prisoner doing a stretch is serving time, i.e. inside
done by the book means done correctly, i.e. right

explanation.surface: Someone serving a prison sentence who nonetheless follows every rule to the letter.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a convict; the definition is the single word 'Player'.
explanation.definitionFit: An inside right is a forward position in old football formations, so a player who fills it.

clue.text: Nettle and grass

definitions.meaning: to nettle is to annoy or irritate
a grass is a police informer

explanation.surface: Two plants growing side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: To nark is to irritate someone; a nark is also slang for an informer.

clue.text: One is a leader in Mosque

definitions.text: One is a leader in Mosque

parts.note: one speaking of themselves says I'm, i.e. I am

indicators.note: the leader of the word Mosque is its first letter

explanation.surface: A statement that someone leads prayers at a mosque.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader in' takes M from 'Mosque'. The whole clue also defines.
explanation.definitionFit: An imam leads the prayers in a mosque, so is a religious leader there.

clue.text: Heading to university for party in his city centre, doge of good breeding

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside another
taking just the centre of the city's name means dropping its outer letters

parts.note: the doge's city is Venice, ruled by doges

indicators.note: one piece goes in place of the other, as in 'swapped for'

parts.note: taken as the word doge
a do is a party

indicators.note: the heading of university is its first letter

explanation.surface: A Venetian doge of good stock, with a university starting point for a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his city' leans on 'doge': doges ruled Venice. 'Heading to university for party' is a swap signalled by 'for'; 'centre' trims the city and 'in' nests the result inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugenic relates to improving inherited qualities through selective breeding.

clue.text: Flavour of the month, having nailed business image

indicators.note: having nailed means having fixed a piece inside

parts.note: something in fashion is in
CO, abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A trendy figure who has secured a business deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having nailed' looks like success in business, but it signals one piece held inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is a picture or image, as in a religious painting or a symbol on screen.

clue.text: Arm and leg finally received by Attila?

indicators.note: received by means held inside the other piece

parts.note: Attila the Hun, so a Hun

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of leg

explanation.surface: Attila the Hun is presented with an arm and a leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attila?' is a definition by example, flagged by the question mark. 'finally' picks the end of 'leg' and 'received by' puts the pieces inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Arms are weapons, and a pistol is a small firearm, an example of one.

clue.text: Frustrate plot the writer's kept hidden?

parts.note: something kept hidden is under the counter, so the writer's possession sits under the shop counter in this down light
the writer's means mine, the setter speaking

explanation.surface: Thwarting a scheme the author has been keeping secret.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry MINE is under COUNTER, i.e. 'under the counter', kept hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: To countermine is to foil a scheme with a counterplot; originally to dig a tunnel to intercept an enemy's mine.

clue.text: After a foul place to go for kicks

definitions.text: After a foul place to go for kicks

parts.words: After a foul place to go for kicks
parts.note: after a foul in the area, footballers go to this marked place to take a kick at goal; the surface suggests a seedy spot for thrills

explanation.surface: A sleazy venue for cheap thrills.
explanation.walkthrough: Read with a comma after 'foul': after a foul, the place where a footballer goes to kick.
explanation.definitionFit: In football the spot twelve yards from goal where a kick awarded for a foul is taken.

clue.text: Habit of the Queen, perhaps, to take a turn loading twelve-bores

indicators.note: taking a turn means the hidden letters are read from right to left
the shotguns are loading, i.e. holding, the letters within their name

explanation.surface: A royal habit of turning while carrying loaded shotguns, as if at a shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loading' signals letters held inside 'twelve-bores'; 'to take a turn' turns those letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit is a garment such as a monk's; a monarch's ceremonial gown is an example of one.

clue.text: This baker is to start new project

parts.note: the word baker is what you get when the letters of break are ground, i.e. crushed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A baker who is about to launch a new venture.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as an instruction, with 'ground' as the anagram signal acting on BREAK, and it produces the word 'baker'.
explanation.definitionFit: To break ground is an idiom for beginning a building job or new undertaking.

clue.text: Cut short year's entry for a bit of old India

indicators.note: cutting short means the last letter of the record is dropped

parts.note: an annal is the record of a single year's events

explanation.surface: An abridged diary entry for one year about colonial India.
explanation.definitionFit: The anna was a coin of British India, worth a sixteenth of a rupee, hence a bit of old currency.

clue.text: One's to produce picture internally, for first of stars contracted influenza

indicators.note: one piece replaces the first letter of the other

parts.note: the stars in a newspaper are the horoscope

indicators.note: contracted means the word influenza is shortened to its familiar clipped form

parts.note: taken as the word influenza

explanation.surface: A star who caught influenza needs an internal scan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contracted' looks like 'caught' but means shortened, so FLU.
explanation.definitionFit: A fluoroscope is an X-ray instrument showing live images of the inside of the body.

clue.text: Surprising end result chap secured in the Open

indicators.note: secured means held inside the other letters
a surprising outcome is an unexpected arrangement, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: a chap is a he

explanation.surface: A golfer's surprising final result in the Open championship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Open' looks like the golf championship; 'Surprising' scrambles END RESULT and 'secured' puts HE inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Without shelter or cover means exposed outdoors, that is out in the open.

clue.text: Top actors Rickman and Firth getting fat

indicators.note: topping each name removes its head, the first letter of Alan and of Colin

parts.note: Alan Rickman, the actor
Colin Firth, the actor

explanation.surface: Two leading British actors putting on weight for a role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' beheads both first names, ALAN and COLIN, leaving LAN and OLIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanolin is the greasy wax from sheep's wool, a fatty substance used in creams.

clue.text: Injury writ large after this vox pop escalated

parts.words: Injury writ large after this vox pop escalated
parts.note: a lesion is an injury: write L for large after this word, then read it upwards and lesion appears; the words in between are the definition

explanation.surface: A journalist's street interviews about an injury grew louder and louder.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: answer plus L (large) turned up ('escalated' in a down entry) gives LESION.
explanation.definitionFit: Vox pop is the voice of the people, and a voice is a sound, so a noise.

clue.text: Glam rockers back at top of class; we're at back!

indicators.note: back means the band's name is turned round

parts.note: Mud were a 1970s British glam rock band
the top of the class is the best pupil

explanation.surface: Pupils who idolise glam rock bands sit at the back of the class.
explanation.walkthrough: Mud had a 1974 Christmas number one. The definition is the cheeky claim of the least able pupils, traditionally seated at the back of the classroom.
explanation.definitionFit: The least clever pupils are stereotypically seated at the rear of a classroom, so they might say this.

clue.text: Work load then left for me?

definitions.text: Work load then left for me?

indicators.note: to work something is to knead or reshape it, so the letters of load are reshaped

parts.note: L, abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that all the work has been left to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' looks like a noun paired with 'load' but is the anagram signal acting on 'load'.
explanation.definitionFit: A factotum or general servant who handles every task, all the jobs left for one person.

clue.text: Pass over stretch of canal

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
on as in 'on top of', meaning over

explanation.surface: Travelling along a length of waterway after crossing a pass.
explanation.walkthrough: The canal is the alimentary canal, not a waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: The large intestine is a section of the alimentary canal, the digestive tract.

clue.text: From which ricocheted the outer shot?

definitions.text: From which ricocheted the outer shot?

indicators.note: with the outer letters shot, i.e. got rid of, only the core of ricocheted remains

explanation.surface: A darts player's throw bounces off the outer ring of the board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the outer shot' removes RIC and TED from either end of 'ricocheted'; the whole clue also describes the line darts are thrown from.
explanation.definitionFit: In darts the oche is the line behind which a player stands to throw, so where shots come from.

clue.text: Pastry case — it's missing: I go after Joel

indicators.note: missing means those letters are taken away from the pastry

parts.note: a samosa is a fried pastry case with a filling
'it' is crossword slang for sex appeal, SA, so it's = SA

explanation.surface: A pastry shell has gone missing and someone follows a man called Joel.
explanation.walkthrough: SA is removed scattered: the S at the start and the A at the end of SAMOSA. 'Joel' looks like a person but is the Old Testament book.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible the book of the prophet who comes immediately after Joel is named for him.

clue.text: A small part to play — 'Tra-la' with this song

indicators.note: to play signals the letters are rearranged, as in playing around with them

parts.note: taken as written, the composite fodder
taken as written, the letters to be found alongside the answer

explanation.surface: An actor with a bit part that consists of singing 'tra-la'.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the letters of A SMALL PART, rearranged ('to play'), equal TRA-LA plus the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalm is a sacred song or hymn, as in the Book of Psalms.

clue.text: Half-inch nail only at intervals runs all the way to the top

indicators.note: going to the top in a down entry means reading the letters upwards
at intervals means every other letter of the words is taken

parts.note: R, cricket abbreviation for runs
up as in 'eat it up', completely

explanation.surface: A half-inch nail, with every other piece missing, ladders up a structure.
explanation.walkthrough: Half-inch is Cockney rhyming slang for pinch, i.e. steal. 'at intervals' takes alternate letters and 'to the top' reads everything upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Half-inch rhymes with pinch, slang for to steal, the same as filch or nick.

clue.text: 'Like some marrow?', I say — look at that interrupting breakfast celebration

parts.note: my! is an exclamation like 'I say'

indicators.note: interrupting means one piece breaks into the other

parts.note: Eid al-Fitr celebrates breaking the Ramadan fast, a break-fast feast
lo means look, behold

explanation.surface: Someone exclaiming over a vegetable during a breakfast party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breakfast' is break-fast: Eid ends a fast. 'Marrow' is bone marrow, not the vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Myeloid describes tissue of or resembling bone marrow, from which blood cells form.

clue.text: Intelligence scores dismal, approaching zero, skew

indicators.note: the rest comes up to the O from behind, so O stands first

parts.note: zero looks like the letter O

indicators.note: to score is to cut into, so the intelligence measure cuts into the other word

parts.note: feeling blue means feeling dismal
IQ, intelligence quotient

explanation.surface: Someone's intelligence test results are so poor they are close to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scores' looks like test marks but means cuts into; 'approaching' puts the zero first.
explanation.definitionFit: Oblique means slanting or at an angle, the same sense as skew.

clue.text: Geneticist driving pupil longing to control second floor

parts.note: L for learner driver

indicators.note: to control is to hold, so the longing holds the second

parts.note: a yen is a longing
S, abbreviation for second
to floor an opponent is to knock them out, KO

explanation.surface: A learner driver yearning to take charge of the second floor of a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'floor' is not a storey but a verb, as in a boxer floored, so KO.
explanation.definitionFit: Trofim Lysenko was a Soviet biologist whose discredited theories of heredity dominated Soviet genetics.

clue.text: Ancient Rimer's associates croaked

definitions.meaning: the sailors aboard with Coleridge's Ancient Mariner in The Rime of the Ancient Mariner
an old past tense of crow, a bird calling harshly, so it called as a croaking bird does

explanation.surface: An old poet's companions all died.
explanation.walkthrough: Coleridge's poem is spelt 'Rime', hence 'Rimer'. The Mariner's shipmates also famously all croaked, i.e. died, in the poem.
explanation.definitionFit: The ship's company of the poem's vessel, and an archaic past form of the verb for a cockerel calling.

clue.text: Arm section to infiltrate all-powerful nation

indicators.note: the answer infiltrates, sitting inside, the words that follow

explanation.surface: A unit of an armed force to infiltrate a superpower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to infiltrate' marks letters inside 'powerful nation'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the two forearm bones, so a part of the arm.

clue.text: One will depart parish and use false god

indicators.note: departing means the word one leaves the district

parts.note: a parish is a district or zone
taken as the word one

indicators.note: false means the letters of use are falsified, rearranged

explanation.surface: A churchgoer will leave the parish and worship a false deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will depart' takes ONE from ZONE leaving Z; 'false' rearranges USE. 'false god' looks like the definition but 'false' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeus was the chief deity of the ancient Greek pantheon.

clue.text: Is this opened by White Rabbit and Hare, say, limping?

definitions.meaning: in chess White makes the first move, opening the match
rabbits and hares are examples of animals hunted for food
a lame leg is called a gammy or bad leg

explanation.surface: Alice's White Rabbit and the March Hare, perhaps, limping along.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions; the Alice in Wonderland picture hides chess.
explanation.definitionFit: A chess match is one, hunted animals are another sense, and a crippled leg is described with this word.

clue.text: Maximise efforts to serve a mug each

parts.note: to do someone, as in 'do breakfast', is to serve them
in scores, 'all' means each, as in fifteen-all
a means one
a can is a drinking vessel, like a mug

explanation.surface: A host serving everyone a single mug of something.
explanation.walkthrough: GO ALL OUT FOR is a tempting wrong answer to 'Maximise efforts'.
explanation.definitionFit: To try as hard as possible is the same as making your efforts as great as they can be.

clue.text: Like four-and-twenty blackbirds? And magpies!

definitions.meaning: baked in a pie, as in the nursery rhyme Sing a Song of Sixpence
like magpies, i.e. black and white in patches

explanation.surface: Comparing nursery-rhyme blackbirds with magpies.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyme's birds were baked in a pie; and the word also describes the patched black-and-white plumage magpies have.

clue.text: Tinned soup, initially cold, through action got intensely hot

parts.note: tinned means in a can

indicators.note: the deed runs through the soup and cold letters, enclosing them

parts.note: a deed is an action

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of soup

parts.note: C, abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Canned soup that started cold has been heated right through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes S from 'soup'; 'through' puts S and C inside DEED.
explanation.definitionFit: To incandesce is to glow with heat, so to have become white-hot or intensely hot.
